newsitem.title: HUNGARY: SPATE OF SMALL BOMBS IN HUNGARY MAY CONTINUE - POLICE.
newsitem.headline: SPATE OF SMALL BOMBS IN HUNGARY MAY CONTINUE - POLICE.

text.p: A pipe bomb which exploded in a parking lot in western Hungary was the fourth this month in a spate of small blasts which police said on Wednesday may continue.
The pipe bomb went off in a parking lot on Tuesday night in Veszprem, damaging several cars but causing no injuries, police said. It was the fourth explosion since October 5.
The Magyar Hirlap newspaper said on Tuesday that police had investigated 28 blasts in the past seven years while as many as 13 hand grenades and other devices have exploded so far this year.
Hungarian national police spokesman Andras Ruzsa said the recent spate could continue.
"The press gives blanket coverage of these explosions," Ruzsa told Reuters. "Perhaps it shouldn't...Young men, people who are inclined to do such things read it and they may happen to try it."
On Saturday night a Slovak youth was killed by a blast in Budapest and the Hungarian and the Slovak police are trying to establish whether it was suicide.

A week ago another bomb exploded in Budapest in a dustbin near Europe's largest synagogue, raising concerns in the Jewish community since it was the second blast in the vicinity of the synagogue since August 25.
And police said on Tuesday they had detained a 17-year-old man who confessed to planting a bomb under a seat in a bus earlier this month in northern Hungary.
The blast injured four people and police said the fact that the doors were open at the time prevented more serious injury.

Ruzsa said suicide or revenge, often between criminal gangs, were the most typical motivation of bomb blasts in Hungary in the past few years, adding that police had no evidence of terrorist groups working in the country.
He said the police also had no evidence of political or religious motivations for the blasts.
